Investigated: NOT two data models as the ticket assumed — both /offboarding/fnf (FnFController->FnFCalculationService) and /offboarding/[id]/fnf (ExitManagementController->ExitManagementService) already read/write the SAME FullAndFinalSettlement entity/table via FullAndFinalSettlementRepository. The real duplication was two independent service-layer implementations of create+approve with no coordination: FnFCalculationService is canonical (has the actual statutory gratuity calc incl. 240-day rule, auto-computation, and a real status-guarded approve); ExitManagementService's settlement methods were thin manual CRUD with NO duplicate-row guard on create and NO status guard on approve (could approve from any status). Consolidated: added a duplicate-settlement guard to ExitManagementService.createSettlement (exitProcessId is meant to be 1:1), and made approveSettlement delegate to FnFCalculationService.approve for the one status-guarded state machine instead of duplicating it. Both controllers/frontend surfaces keep working unchanged. Found a third redundant frontend page (/offboarding/exit/fnf, raw fetch calls bypassing fnf.service.ts) not mentioned in the ticket - flagging for frontend, not touched.

Decision: formalize the split, don't merge. Full merge would require reconciling two different response DTOs (FullAndFinalSettlementResponse vs FnFCalculationResponse) each with live frontend consumers, for no added safety — the one path where divergence was dangerous (approval) is already consolidated onto FnFCalculationService.approve from the prior story. Documented ownership boundaries in both services' javadoc/comments: FnFCalculationService is canonical for calc+approval, ExitManagementService's settlement methods are a secondary writer that must delegate to it for anything cross-cutting.

Chose lowest-risk fix: added ownership check (enforceMeetingViewScope, same shape as FeedbackController.enforceFeedbackViewScope) to the legacy MeetingController.getByEmployee instead of repointing frontend. Repointing was rejected: the secured OneOnOneMeetingController is a much richer, differently-shaped API (own DTOs, agenda/actions/dashboard) not a drop-in swap, and frontend already calls both controllers for different features. Allows self, the employee's manager (via getAllReporteeIds), or HR/admin scope; denies everyone else.

Replaced raw @RequestBody OneOnOneMeeting entity binding on scheduleMeeting with the existing OneOnOneMeetingRequest DTO (already used by the secured OneOnOneMeetingController for the same entity), so a client can no longer set id/tenantId/status/audit fields or other employees' notes at creation time. managerId is now derived from SecurityContext.getCurrentEmployeeId(), not client input. Backward compatible: Jackson ignores unknown JSON properties, so the current frontend payload (built from the full OneOnOneMeetingEntity shape) still deserializes fine, just with the illegitimate fields silently dropped instead of persisted.
